subject: Pegasus AI renewal — pragmatic rightsize + transient GPU buffer request
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.ch@mail.redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@mail.redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@mail.redwood.ai>

Subject: Renewal conversation — sizing options and a small transient buffer

Hi Samira / Carlos,

Thanks again for the review last week. We pulled the Q3 utilization slices and put together a pragmatic set of options for your upcoming renewal. Key point up front: Pegasus spent 62% of its provisioned fleet on steady production inference, with clear mid-day spikes that pushed peak utilization to ~88% for several hours on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Those spikes are where you saw the latency alerts.

Attached: pegagus_usage_q3.csv (summary), proposed_commit_table.xlsx (3 commit variants), sow_amendment_draft.pdf (redline-ready).

Options we recommend (brief):
- Option A: Rightsize commit to 70% of current provisioned capacity (saves ~18% monthly) + 10% transient buffer pool (burstable, pay-as-used)
- Option B: Keep current commit but add 15% guaranteed burst capacity (better SLA)
- Option C: Conservative top-up: +8 GPUs now, review after 8 weeks with telemetry-based rollback option

Questions for you: procurement timeline, whether you want guaranteed burst (Option B) vs. pay-as-used buffer (Option A), and if legal needs a tracked redline on the SOW.

Next steps: If you confirm procurement timeline I’ll loop in Sales Ops to prepare the amendment and get pricing for each option.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: pegagus_usage_q3.csv, proposed_commit_table.xlsx, sow_amendment_draft.pdf)

Irene — thanks for this. Quick clarifying Qs before we escalate to procurement:

1) Can you break down the monthly cost delta for Option A vs Option B (line item: base commit cost, burst compute, and estimated data transfer)?
2) The transient buffer in Option A — how is that billed (per-minute per-GPU or per-hour slices)?
3) If we pick Option C (top-up + review), what’s the process and lead time to reduce the top-up if usage drops?

Procurement timeline: likely a 3–4 week review. We need the pricing breakdown and a tracked SOW redline to move.

—Carlos
VP Engineering, Pegasus AI

Carlos — quick answers, attaching a compact pricing table (proposed_commit_table.xlsx) and the cost delta lines you asked for. High level:

- Option A (rightsize + pay-as-used buffer): lowest committed cost, highest variability in month-to-month bill but predictable peak handling. Buffer billed in 15-minute increments.
- Option B (keep commit + guaranteed burst): higher committed spend but capped burst charges; best for strict latency SLAs.
- Option C (incremental top-up + telemetry review): operationally simplest for an 8-week runway; removal of top-up requires a 30-day notice once telemetry shows stable utilization below threshold.

I’ll call out numbers in the sheet, but ballpark: Option A reduces committed spend by ~17% vs current, with estimated buffer charges of 2–6% of current spend depending on spike frequency. Option B increases committed spend by ~9% but keeps buffer charges under 1%. Option C is +6% now with a potential rollback after the 8-week window.

If procurement needs the SOW redline, Marissa can drive that with Legal; copying her.

Ben
Principal Growth Account Executive
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: proposed_commit_table.xlsx)

- If we do Option A, can Redwood provide a soft cap (billing alert + automatic fallback to cheaper model variant) when buffer usage exceeds an agreed monthly threshold?

Procurement window: we’re targeting sign by Nov 18 (3.5 weeks). Please send the percentile forecast and the SOW redline by EoD Oct 25 if possible.

Samira — quick technical note on the buffer behavior and mitigation controls we can offer: 

- Forecasts: Attached is a 90th/95th percentile projection over the next 8 weeks based on your Q3 cadence (we used 15-min buckets). Expected buffer draw at the 95th percentile is ~12 GPUs sustained for ~3 hours on peak days; 90th percentile is ~6 GPUs.
- Billing granularity: buffers bill in 15-minute increments with per-minute metering internally; line items will show on the monthly invoice as "transient burst".
- Soft cap & automation: we can enable a soft spend alert at a threshold you set (email + Slack). If the soft cap is breached repeatedly in a 7-day window, we can automatically switch overflow traffic to a lower-cost model variant (model fallback) and throttle non-critical routing. This will be captured in the SOW amendment.
- Rollback mechanics for Option C: once telemetry shows P50 utilization <60% for a 30-day rolling window we can remove the top-up with 30 days' notice; the telemetry and API hooks will be explicitly documented.

I’ve uploaded the percentile CSV to the shared Drive link. If Procurement needs a sample invoice line we can provide one for the first month.

Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: pegasus_percentiles_90_95.csv)
